title: The Stars of the Milky Way
caption: The Milky Way over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way rises above ESO's La Silla Observatory, its bright band dotted with red star-forming regions and woven with dark filaments of dust. Two of the site's telescopes are in view: the 1-metre Schmidt telescope on the left and the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope on the right. Just above the 2.2-metre, towards the centre-right, is the Large Magellanic Cloud, a neighbouring dwarf galaxy, and a pink and green glow of airglow hangs just over the horizon.

Every star in the sky belongs to our galaxy, so why call only this streak the Milky Way? Our galaxy is shaped like a giant pancake with a bright central bulge, and nearly all its stars, gas and dust lie in a thin disc. The Solar System sits on one spiral arm, roughly two-thirds of the way out from the centre. The bright band is our view along that disc, looking in towards the crowded centre.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph at ESO's La Silla Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A camera exposure can gather far more light than the eye, so the red star-forming regions and the airglow may look more vivid than they would to someone on site.
